verdicts.text: Adopted premises type the uniform-lapse (k=0) mode as a constraint (fixed-H / fixed-preparation null direction; time reparametrization; global energy and homogeneous data from the separate background/normal-constraint solve). The canonical -beta Var(H) value is the counted computational branch (CA-34), not a premise.
k=0 typing alone does not decide the 1/r tail; the far field is the k->0+ limit of the k!=0 kernel. In CA-28 that limit is grid[0,0,0] (1-w0=(L^2-1)/12 sum q^2), contradicting CRS:33.

Schur bound: T(k)<=0 on (0,kappa_1) for any NSD-source typing; 0 violations on ~98k premise points per typing (25 admissible estimates); violations only in the gate-violating RD3 probe (44956 points).
Every measured typing (37 estimates x 13 rays) gives finite reach or a repulsive power law; no attractive tail in any gate-consistent typing.

Attractive Newtonian tail needs C1 (F_nn(0+)=0) AND C2 (vanishing native uniform chart stiffness). C2 alone with isothermal lapse gives a real-k pole at k_p=sqrt(4 pi G Qinf/(c^4 |T(0)|)) (|T(0)|=T_EH(k_p), <=1.2%) and finite repulsive T(0+). Corrects H4 v3/section 6 and V4A A39 item 4.
Qinf=c^4/(16 pi G gamma_eff)=8.0623 unchanged by every typing (|Q(1000/kpc)/Qinf-1|<=8.1e-9); A21 short-wavelength shifts <=2.1e-4 at |k|>=2/kpc (continuation), <=4.8e-5 (lapse-only).

Existence of a 1/r tail: decided by U1 (small-k limit of k!=0 lapse and chart entries, mixed L>=6) and U2 (energy relaxation at k_g vs galaxy age). Within CA-28 only finite / 1/r / linear far fields are representable; other forms need a non-analytic infinite-volume response (UNTESTED, LIVE:41).
